question: What will be the nationwide wastewater detection category of enterovirus D68 on December 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: WastewaterSCAN national EV-D68 category is High (Sept 2026 update: ~72% detection, among the highest concentrations since 2023; reportedly still High in late Oct). Wave onset was mid-Sept 2026, ~6 weeks later than 2024. Seasonal categories use onset/offset: Low requires >50% of sites in offset. Analogs: the 2025 Midwest wave lasted ~11 weeks (mid-Aug to Nov); 2024 was Low by Jan 2025 with December median below LOD. An 11-week wave from mid-Sept ends around Dec 1, so offset could be declared by then, but offset detection lags and the West may come late, which favors High persisting. Medium is rare under this scheme. No human market found (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers).
calls.dossier:
- WWSCAN Sept 2026 update (pub 2026-10-02): EV-D68 national category HIGH; detected in ~72% of samples in Sept vs ~20% in Aug; median 8,864 copies/g (Aug below LOD); among the highest concentrations since monitoring began Sept 2023; elevated detections across Midwest, Northeast and South since mid-Sept; West lower, though Bay Area sites (Palo Alto, Napa, SE SF, San Rafael) were high and rising in early Oct (hoodline 2026-10-06). WWSCAN says EV-D68 'typically circulates late summer/early fall, major outbreaks biennially'.
- A search snippet (unverified page) said the national category was still HIGH as of 2026-10-23. Iowa epi update 2026-10-16: national wastewater EV-D68 increases 'in recent weeks'. No source found showing a national decline as of late Oct 2026. The October 2026 monthly update was not yet published (normally appears early in the next month; the Nov 2026 update would come in early Dec).
- Category method (WWSCAN Nov/Dec 2025 updates): EV-D68 is treated as a seasonal pathogen 'rarely detected outside of season/outbreaks'. National LOW when >50% of sites are in seasonal offset; HIGH when >50% are in onset (or on high concentrations, per the Sept 2026 wording). Categories combine 21-day trend, level vs national tertiles, and detection frequency. Site counts Oct-Dec 2025: MEDIUM = 0 sites every month (e.g. Dec 2025: 99 LOW / 0 MED / 22 HIGH / 26 insufficient data).
- 2025 (off-year): Midwest elevated from mid-Aug 2025, declined by Nov; West rose from late Sept. National LOW in Oct, Nov and Dec 2025 (~28% detection); West region HIGH in Dec 2025.
- 2024 (major wave, all 4 regions): rising from early Aug 2024; Sept 2024 national 'Medium' under the older detection-based method; switched to seasonal classification 2024-10-15; Bay Area SCAN sites HIGH as of 2024-11-13; one summary said concentrations plateaued early Nov to late Dec 2024, yet the Dec 2024 national median was below LOD; Jan 2025 national LOW (~21% detection, mostly California). The national category on ~Dec 1, 2024 was searched for but not found.
- 2026 onset (mid-Sept) is ~6 weeks later than 2024 (early Aug). Dec 1, 2026 is ~11 weeks after the 2026 onset.
- Resolves off the WastewaterSCAN dashboard national EV-D68 category as first displayed on/after 2026-12-01 (backup: the wwscan.ghost.io monthly update); Not Detected/Not Calculated -> Other. Not CDC NWSS.
- Event window: single-point reading on/after 2026-12-01; as of 2026-10-29, ~33 days remain.
- Searched, not found: Nov/Dec 2024 national updates; offset-timing details in the medRxiv EV-D68 wastewater paper (403); the live dashboard value (JS-rendered). No human prediction market found.

In 2024 (the biennial outbreak year, onset early Aug) the national median was below LOD by Dec and LOW by Jan 2025; 2025 stayed LOW Oct-Dec. The 2026 onset was later (mid-Sept) and larger, so in-season status could last to Dec 1, but peak-and-decline by late Nov is the typical pattern. calls.reasoning: Status quo: the national EV-D68 category is HIGH (Sept 2026 update, 72% of samples positive, among the highest concentrations since 2023). The latest post on wwscan.ghost.io is still the Sept update. The only analog is 2024: onset in early Aug, Medium in early Oct, and (per Run 3, which I could not verify) Low by Nov 22 2024 even at ~57% detection. The 2026 onset came ~4-6 weeks later (mid-Sept). That puts Dec 1 2026 about 11 weeks into the wave, roughly where mid-to-late Oct 2024 was, when the category was still Medium or High. That favors High/Medium holding over a quick drop to Low. Against that: EV-D68 waves typically peak Sep-Oct, and once a majority of sites enter seasonal offset the category flips to LOW, so Low stays live. Medium is less likely because sites tend to be either offset (Low) or in onset at a high level, though a declining trend could produce it. Other is small because offset displays as LOW, not Not Calculated. No human market found.

calls.reconciliation: The runs disagree mainly on judgment: how fast the category falls after the peak. The factual premises in dispute were (a) whether the national category is still High in late Oct 2026, and (b) the 2024 path (Medium in early Oct, Low by Nov 22 and Dec 20). Checks: ghost.io's latest post is still the Sept 2026 update (HIGH), with no October update yet. My late-Oct trend search found only early-Oct reports of a rising trend and nothing showing a decline. The Nov 2024 update URL returned 404, and the 2024 figures could not be verified by search, so I accept Run 3's 2024 path as plausible but unverified. Lining up timing from onset rather than calendar date, Dec 1 2026 falls about where Oct 2024 sat, which favors High/Medium more than Run 3 allowed. The fact that Low arrived within ~16 weeks in 2024 keeps Low substantial. I carry forward the shared reference class.
